name: Patchline reviewer skills taxonomy
claim: Patchline publishes a public reviewer skills taxonomy that maps gate-backed data-change hazard classes to concepts reviewers must understand, prerequisite knowledge, assessment prompts, evidence hashes, role-specific tutorial crosswalks, certification scenarios, and negative controls. The taxonomy is deliberately executable: missing evidence, missing gates, weak prerequisites, and uncrosswalked hazard classes become deterministic counterexamples instead of silently becoming curriculum drift.

concepts.title: Prove every legacy row is covered before a contract step
concepts.description: Reviewer can explain why a NOT NULL or compatibility-code deletion must wait for complete replay-store evidence.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Use the staged backfill plan to decide whether the contract stage can proceed and cite the missing-row negative control.

concepts.title: Separate expand, backfill, contract, and cleanup evidence
concepts.description: Reviewer can distinguish a safe staged contract from a patch that deletes compatibility code too early.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Name the proof that blocks compatibility-code deletion until validation is exhaustive.

negative_controls.mutation: Use the incomplete replay store so one legacy invoice has no target value.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: contract and compatibility deletion remain blocked with the missing row witness

hazard_classes.title: Representative workload regression from schema changes

concepts.title: Compare before/after representative query shapes
concepts.description: Reviewer can identify when an index or column change requires qualitative workload checks.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Explain why the gate reports qualitative plan-shape risk without inventing measured EXPLAIN costs.

concepts.title: Refuse unmeasured cost claims
concepts.description: Reviewer can separate static plan-shape evidence from measured database runtime claims.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Identify which checks must hand off to db-dry-run before a measured performance claim is allowed.

negative_controls.mutation: Replace a query-plan regression case with a plain ADD COLUMN control.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the detector stays quiet instead of fabricating a regression

concepts.title: Recognize adapter-specific safety obligations
concepts.description: Reviewer can distinguish pt-osc, gh-ost, native concurrent indexes, and framework helpers from ordinary DDL.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Name the trigger, binlog, or cutover obligation that makes the adapter reviewable.

concepts.title: Review cutover and rollback gaps
concepts.description: Reviewer can explain why non-atomic online migration phases still require explicit rollback and validation.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Use the adapter fixture to list the cutover obligations that must be reviewed manually.

negative_controls.mutation: Remove the adapter marker from an otherwise ordinary ALTER TABLE fixture.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the detector does not classify the statement as online schema change

hazard_classes.title: Broad retention and privacy-impact data change

concepts.title: Identify broad deletes, anonymization, and export retention hazards
concepts.description: Reviewer can connect a data-retention change to privacy obligations and review scope.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Classify whether the fixture describes deletion, anonymization, export retention, or rollback-gap risk.

concepts.title: Check rollback evidence for privacy-sensitive broad writes
concepts.description: Reviewer can spot when a privacy-sensitive operation lacks enough rollback or validation evidence.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Explain which rollback or validation obligation is missing from the negative control.

negative_controls.mutation: Replace a broad privacy-sensitive change with a scoped non-sensitive control.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the privacy hazard count does not inflate from ordinary scoped DML

concepts.title: Verify migration jobs are sequenced before dependent deploys
concepts.description: Reviewer can connect Helm hooks, sync waves, init containers, and Terraform dependencies to migration safety.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Use the infra-ordering evidence to explain why a migration job is sequenced or unordered.

concepts.title: Recognize unordered migration job controls
concepts.description: Reviewer can explain why removing an ordering marker should produce an unsafe deployment race.
concepts.assessment_prompt: Name the ordering marker whose removal makes the negative control fail.

negative_controls.mutation: Remove the Helm hook or sync-wave marker from the migration job.
negative_controls.expected_counterexample: the job is classified as unordered and must not be accepted
